title: Deino × Brightkite Logistics: discovery

calendarEvent.title: Deino × Brightkite Logistics: discovery
calendarEvent.description:
Hi Marcus and Hannah,

Looking forward to the call. Rough agenda:
1. How dispatch works at Brightkite today
2. Security and IT requirements
3. Next steps

Join Zoom Meeting: https://deino.zoom.us/j/84213397051

Lena Okafor
Account Executive, Deino

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Hi Marcus, hi Hannah. Thanks so much for making the time today. Can you both hear me okay?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Hi, yeah, I can hear you.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yep, we've got you. I'm in a conference room at our Columbus office, and I think Hannah's at her desk.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Hi, yes. I can hear everyone fine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: How's Columbus this week? Lena said fall showed up early out there.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It did. Forty-five degrees this morning, and the techs are already complaining about frozen dock doors. It's going to be a long winter.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Great. So I've got Shreyas with me, he's our co-founder and CTO. He'll jump in on anything technical, and especially anything security related.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Hi everyone, nice to meet you. Lena's told me a fair bit already, so honestly I'm mostly here to listen today.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Ha, that's the right attitude for a sales call. Good to meet you.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So we've got thirty minutes. My plan was to spend most of it understanding how dispatch works for you today and what's not working.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Then I'd love to hear from Hannah on security requirements, and at the end we can talk about what a sensible next step looks like. Does that work for you both?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That works. Just so you know, I've got a hard stop at the half hour, I have our ops review right after.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Noted, we'll be done on time. So Marcus, maybe start with the big picture. How is the field operation set up today?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Sure. So we've got about two hundred and twenty field technicians, give or take, across three regions. East, Central and West.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And we have fourteen dispatchers in total, so roughly four or five per region. Central is the biggest.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The techs do installs and maintenance on warehouse equipment. Dock levelers, conveyors, doors, that kind of thing. So a job can be forty minutes or it can be a full day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And how does a job come in? Walk me through it from the customer calling to the tech showing up.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Customer calls or emails our service desk, the desk logs a ticket, and the ticket lands with the dispatchers for that region. The dispatcher picks a tech, puts it on the schedule, and texts the tech the details.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: How do dispatchers decide which tech gets a job? Is it just whoever's free, or do skills come into it?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Skills matter a lot. Some techs are certified on specific manufacturers, some can do high-voltage work and some can't. Right now that lives in the dispatchers' heads, honestly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So if your most experienced dispatcher is out sick, that knowledge is out sick too.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Pretty much. Last winter we sent an uncertified tech to the same kind of job twice in one week because the regular dispatcher was on vacation.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We store certifications per tech and the board can filter on them, so the dispatcher only sees techs who can actually do the job.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That alone would help a lot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the schedule itself lives where?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Honestly, a mix. We've got DispatchPro 6, which is an on-prem tool we've had for, I want to say, nine years. And then on top of that every region has its own spreadsheets, because DispatchPro doesn't do half the things we need.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Which one is the real source of truth, the spreadsheet or DispatchPro?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Depends who you ask. Officially DispatchPro. In practice it's the spreadsheet, and then somebody re-keys it into DispatchPro at the end of the day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Got it. And what's driving the conversation now? Why look at this now and not, say, a year ago?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Couple of things. The big one is that the DispatchPro licence ends on the thirty-first of January, twenty twenty-seven.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And the vendor has basically told us version six is end of life. So either we pay for a migration to their new cloud product or we move to something else.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And frankly, the cloud product is not cheap and it's not great. We had a demo, it was the same screens in a browser.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So January thirty-first is a real deadline for you.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's a real deadline. I do not want to be running dispatch off spreadsheets alone in February.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Understood. And beyond the licence, what are the day-to-day pains? If I sat next to one of your dispatchers for a morning, what would I see go wrong?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Double-booking is the one that drives me crazy. Two dispatchers in the same region put the same tech on two jobs at nine because one of them was looking at a stale copy of the sheet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Then the tech goes to one of them, and the other customer calls us at nine thirty asking where he is.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: How often does that happen, roughly?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Um, a few times a week per region? It's not every day. But it's often enough that customers notice and bring it up in QBRs.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The second one is drive time. We've got techs crossing regions because whoever was free got assigned.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I've seen a West tech drive two and a half hours for a job that a Central tech was twenty minutes from. That's half a day gone.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Because each dispatcher only really sees their own region's sheet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Exactly. Nobody has the full picture across the three regions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And the third thing is visibility. Once a tech leaves the depot we kind of lose them. We don't know if a job started, if it's running long, if he's stuck in traffic.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The dispatcher usually finds out when the next customer calls to complain.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So job status today is basically phone calls and texts?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Phone calls, texts, and some of the guys are good about posting in a group chat. Some are, uh, not good about it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Do the techs have company phones? And what are they on for calendars and email?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Company phones, Android mostly, a few iPhones. And we're on Microsoft 365, so everybody's got Outlook.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Okay, good, that's one we sync with today. Techs get their jobs in our mobile app, and if they want, the jobs also show up in their Outlook calendar.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That would be popular. Half of them live in Outlook anyway because of the HR stuff.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Okay. Let me try to put some numbers on this, because it really helps when we put a proposal together. How many jobs does a dispatcher handle in a day?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Each dispatcher handles around sixty jobs a day. Some days more, Mondays are always worse.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Sixty per dispatcher, fourteen dispatchers. So you're somewhere north of eight hundred jobs a day across the company.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yeah, about that, on a normal day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And how many of those end up getting moved? Rescheduled, reassigned, pushed to another day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We actually looked at this last quarter, because I wanted to know. We estimate about eleven percent of jobs get rescheduled at least once.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And that's only the ones we caught. Some spreadsheet changes never make it back into DispatchPro, so the real number is probably higher.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Eleven percent of eight hundred is a lot of phone calls every day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's a lot of phone calls. And every one of those is a dispatcher doing it by hand. Call the tech, call the customer, update two systems, hope nobody else touched the sheet in the meantime.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Is there a cost you attach to that internally? Overtime, missed SLAs, anything like that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We have SLAs with about a third of our customers, four-hour response on breakdowns. We paid out service credits on a couple of accounts last quarter.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I don't have a clean dollar figure, and I'd rather not quote you one I'd have to walk back later.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's completely fair. The sixty jobs and the eleven percent are already really useful.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Okay, switching gears a little. How does a decision like this get made at Brightkite? Who besides the two of you is involved?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Operationally it's my call. I own dispatch and field ops. But anything with a multi-year contract goes through our CFO, so in practice I decide together with the CFO.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And Hannah basically has a veto. If it doesn't pass security, it doesn't happen, no matter how much I like it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That's accurate. I've said no to two tools this year already.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Good to know. And on budget timing?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We do budget approval in November for the following year. So if we want this funded for twenty twenty-seven, it needs to be in the November cycle.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So working backwards: budget approval in November, DispatchPro switched off at the end of January. That suggests you'd want to have tried something real before November.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Ideally, yes. I don't want to walk into the CFO's office with a slide deck. I want to walk in with "we ran it in one region and here's what happened."

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's exactly where I was hoping to go. Let's come back to that in a minute, because I want to give Hannah proper time first.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Hannah, do you want to walk us through what you need on the security side?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Sure. I'll keep it short, because I'll send our full vendor security questionnaire anyway.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The non-negotiables are, first, SSO through Okta. We don't allow any vendor app with local passwords. Second, a SOC 2 report.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Third, data residency in the US. All of our data and our customers' data has to stay in the US. And fourth, a summary of your most recent penetration test.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Okay. Let me take those one at a time.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: SSO with Okta, yes. We support SAML and OIDC, and we have customers on Okta today.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We also support SCIM provisioning. So when someone leaves Brightkite and you deprovision them in Okta, they lose access to Deino automatically.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Good. SCIM matters to us. We've had real problems with offboarding at other vendors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: On SOC 2, I want to be precise because I know it matters. We have a SOC 2 Type I report today.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Our Type II observation window starts on the first of November with our auditor, so the Type II report itself comes after that window closes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So you don't have a Type II today.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Correct, not today. I'd rather say that up front than have you find it on page forty of a report.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Okay. For us, Type I is acceptable to start a pilot. For a full contract I'll need to see the Type II timeline in writing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's reasonable. I'll put the timeline in writing in what I send you.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: On data residency, everything runs in AWS in the US. Primary region is us-east-2 in Ohio, and backups go to us-west-2. Nothing leaves the US.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And your sub-processors? Who else touches the data?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They're listed, and I'll include the current list. The ones that touch customer data are all US-hosted.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: What about support access? Do your engineers, or anyone outside the US, have access to production data?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Good question. Production access is limited to a small group, it's just-in-time, and it's logged.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Honestly, our infrastructure and security lead, Priya, should answer the specifics in writing rather than me improvising on a call.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I appreciate that. I'd much rather have it in writing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And on the pen test, we had a third-party test done this summer. I can share the executive summary and the remediation status for each finding.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That's exactly what I need. Executive summary and remediation status.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So Shreyas, you'd bundle all of that up for Hannah?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes. I'll send Hannah a security package: the SOC 2 Type I report, the Type II timeline, the pen-test summary, the sub-processor list, and the data residency details.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I can have that to you by tomorrow, under our standard NDA.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Tomorrow's great. If you send me the NDA, I'll get it signed the same day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I'll send the NDA over to you right after this call.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And I'll send you our vendor security questionnaire. It's about eighty questions, so, sorry in advance.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Ha, we've seen worse. Two hundred is the record so far.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: One more thing, and I want to be really clear about it. No real Brightkite data goes into your system until I've signed off on the security review.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Completely understood. We wouldn't want it any other way.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Oh, hang on one second. Somebody just walked into the room.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Okay, sorry about that. Carlos just joined me here. Carlos runs dispatch for the Central region, he's one of our dispatcher supervisors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I mentioned this call to him this morning, I hope you don't mind him sitting in.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Hi. Sorry to crash your meeting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Not at all, Carlos, really glad you're here. Honestly you're the person we most want to hear from.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We were just talking about double-booking and rescheduling. From where you sit, what does a bad day look like?

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: A bad day is a Monday where three techs call in sick and I have to move, like, twenty jobs before eight in the morning.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Right now that means I'm in the spreadsheet, I'm in DispatchPro, and I'm on the phone at the same time. Usually all three at once.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: What's the slowest part of moving a job?

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: DispatchPro, for sure. Moving one job is like six clicks and a form, and if you get it wrong it doesn't tell you. I just want to grab the job and drop it on another tech.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So drag and drop on a board, with a row per tech and the time slots across the top.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Yeah. Drag it, drop it, and it tells me if I'm creating a conflict before I do it, not after.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's pretty much how our dispatch board works. You drag a job onto a tech's row, and if it overlaps something or the drive time doesn't fit, it flags it before you confirm.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Okay. Yeah, that's the thing I want to see.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: The other thing is I'm not always at my desk. I'm on the floor, I'm out in the yard. I need to see on my phone who's running late.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Late meaning they haven't started the job at the scheduled time?

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Late meaning they're not going to make the next one. If I know at ten that one of my guys is going to be forty minutes late for his eleven o'clock, I can call the customer before the customer calls me.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Got it. Today we flag late starts and jobs that are running over on the dispatch board, and the board works on a tablet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A proper phone view just for supervisors isn't something we have as its own screen yet. I don't want to promise it on a call.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Okay, fair enough. At least you're not overselling it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We'll show you what exists in the demo, and you tell us whether it's close enough or not.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Deal. I'll be honest with you.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: The other thing is my dispatchers are not, like, computer people. Some of them have been on DispatchPro for nine years. If it's complicated, they'll go straight back to the spreadsheet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's a really common worry, and it's a fair one. It's why I want the demo to be for them specifically, on their own kind of week.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And usually in a pilot we do a training session up front, and someone from our side sits on a call with the dispatch team for the first few mornings.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Okay. That would help. The first Monday is going to be rough no matter what.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Since Carlos is here, let me ask the pilot question. I was thinking, why not just do all three regions at once? We've got the January deadline, and I'd rather not do this twice.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I understand the instinct. I'd actually push back a little on that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: If we do all three, you're onboarding two hundred and twenty techs and fourteen dispatchers right in the middle of your budget cycle. And if something goes sideways, it goes sideways everywhere at once.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And the thing you want to show your CFO in November is a clean before and after. One region running on Deino next to two regions that aren't is actually a better comparison.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Hm. Yeah, okay, that's a fair point. The comparison is really what I'd want to show.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So one region. Carlos, Central's about seventy techs, right?

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Seventy-ish. Seventy-two last time I checked.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So the proposal would be one region, seventy technicians, sixty days.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Sixty days gets us to early December if we start mid-October. That's tight but it works.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Okay. One region, seventy techs, sixty days. Let's do that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It'll probably be Central since Carlos is sitting here volunteering, but I want to check with the other two supervisors before I commit to which region.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: I didn't volunteer, I just walked in.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Ha, around here that's the same thing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: How long would onboarding take on our side? Typically we can have a region live in about two weeks after security sign-off, including a training session for the dispatchers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Two weeks is fine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Let's talk money for a second, just so I'm not surprised later. What does this cost?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Sure. Our standard plan is forty-five dollars per technician per month, on an annual contract.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But given what Hannah needs, SSO with Okta and SCIM, you'd be on our enterprise tier, which is sixty dollars per technician per month.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Sixty per tech. So for two-twenty techs that's, what, about a hundred and fifty-eight thousand a year?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: About that at list, yes. For a contract that size there's room to talk about multi-year terms, but I'd rather have that conversation once you've seen the pilot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And the pilot itself. Is that free?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We don't do free pilots, mostly because free pilots don't get the attention they need on either side.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: What we'd do is charge the pilot at the enterprise rate for the seventy techs, and if you sign an annual contract, the pilot fee gets credited against your first year.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Okay, I can live with that. Put it in the proposal and I'll take it to the CFO.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Can I ask a blunt question, though? You're a young company. What happens to us if you're not around in two years?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Totally fair question. We have forty-one paying customers today, we're well funded, and our contracts include a data export clause.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And everything is exportable through the API at any time, not just when a contract ends. We don't hold anyone's data hostage.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Okay. The CFO will ask exactly that, so I wanted to hear it from you directly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Will do. I'll price the proposal on the enterprise tier since you need the SSO anyway.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: A couple of other questions while I have you. Do you do route optimization? Like automatically building out each tech's day?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not today. We show drive times and we flag bad assignments, but automatic route optimization isn't on our roadmap this quarter. I don't want to sell you something that doesn't exist.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Fair. That's a nice-to-have, not a must-have.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And we invoice out of NetSuite. Any integration there?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No native NetSuite integration. We have an API and CSV exports of completed jobs.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I could maybe look at whether our export has the fields your finance team needs, but I wouldn't count on it for the pilot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That's fine. The pilot doesn't need invoicing, we can keep doing that the old way for sixty days.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Sorry, one thing on the mobile app. Is any job data stored on the phone, and is it encrypted?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Jobs are cached on the device so techs can see their day with bad signal, and the cache is encrypted. Sign-in goes through your Okta, and you can revoke a device session from the admin panel.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Okay. Put that in the package too, please.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And audit logs. Do you log admin actions? Who changed a user's role, who exported data, that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes. Admin actions and exports go into an audit log you can see in the admin panel, and on the enterprise tier you can stream it to your SIEM.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Good. We'd want it in our SIEM, so that's another point for the enterprise tier.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Will do, I'll add a section on the mobile app.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: One thing that would really help us make the demo useful. Could you share a sample week of job data, anonymised?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Job types, durations, which tech, which region. We'd load it so your dispatchers see their kind of week and not our generic demo data.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I can do that. I'll strip customer names and addresses. Is a CSV export from DispatchPro okay?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A CSV is perfect.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I'll get you a sample week of anonymised job data by Monday.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Since that's anonymised, I'm okay with it going over before the review. But please send it through our secure file share, not email.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Fine, I'll use the share.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And for the demo, I'd love to do one just for the dispatchers. Carlos and whoever else from his team. We'd show drag-and-drop rescheduling on your own data and the late view on a tablet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Could we do Wednesday the seventh?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Wednesday the seventh works for me. Carlos?

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Mornings are bad for us. Anytime after two is fine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Let's say Wednesday the seventh, two o'clock your time, for an hour. I'll send the invite today.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And Carlos, we'll make sure drag-and-drop rescheduling is front and center.

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Good. That's all I care about, honestly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: We should also think about, uh, whether the West guys want to see it. But let's see how the first demo goes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Okay, we're coming up on time, so let me recap to make sure we're all on the same page.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I'll send a pilot proposal by Friday, October second. One region, seventy techs, sixty days, priced on the enterprise tier with the pilot credit against year one.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Shreyas sends Hannah the security package by tomorrow, and I send the NDA today. Hannah sends us the security questionnaire.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Marcus, you share a sample week of anonymised job data through your secure share by Monday. And we do a tailored demo for the dispatchers on Wednesday the seventh at two your time.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That's it. And I'll confirm which region the pilot runs in before the demo on the seventh.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
